title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer backoff ordering + regional circuit-breaker threshold smoothing
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: Improve SLO enforcer backoff ordering to prevent premature regional failover and smooth circuit-breaker threshold adjustments to avoid oscillation under bursty load.
description:
Context: During a recent regional incident we observed the SLO enforcer aggressively tripping regional circuit-breakers when transient latency spikes occurred. Two root causes were identified: 1) the enforcer backoff queue processed delayed failure signals out-of-order which allowed older high-latency samples to override newer healthy signals; 2) CB threshold smoothing used a simple rolling max that reacted too quickly to bursts, causing oscillation between regions and unnecessary failovers. This hotfix tightens ordering guarantees and introduces a smoothing window + hysteresis to the regional circuit-breaker thresholds.

Changes in this PR: consolidated ordering in the SLO enforcer backoff queue (atomically apply per-region sequence ids), add a short smoothing window and hysteresis when promoting/demoting regional circuit-breaker thresholds, and add guards to prevent simultaneous full failover when a single downstream dependency is degrading. Also includes tests and a temporary metric to monitor smoothing effectiveness.

Why this change: prevent cascading regional failovers and reduce client-facing rate of 502/504 errors during short-lived noisy periods. This is a targeted hotfix that preserves existing backoff semantics while preventing ordering-induced regressions.

Testing: unit tests for ordering semantics and smoothing logic, integration test that replays the incident trace, and a canary rollout to staging. Load test applied 1M requests with injected 250ms 5s burst and verified SLO enforcer did not prematurely failover. CI passed.

Rollout plan: squash-merge to release/2026-03-01, immediate canary to 10% of traffic in us-west-2 for 30 minutes, monitor new metric slo.enforcer.smoothing.applied_count and regional-cb.promote/demote events. If metrics look stable after 30m, promote to 100% for release. Rollback: revert the merge and roll back the canary configuration (traffic switch) if regressions are observed.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: it avoids changing global failover heuristics and only smooths regional decisions. Follow-up work (ENG-7901) will tackle long-term rate-limiter tuning and more sophisticated signal weighting.
